questions.question: Explain the basic function of options in derivatives.
questions.solution_html:
• Options are derivative contracts that give the buyer the right but not the obligation to buy (Call
  • option) or sell (Put option) an underlying asset at a predetermined strike price on or before
  • a specific date. Their basic functions are hedging (protecting against price risk),
  • speculation (betting on price movements with limited downside), and income generation
  • (writing options for premium). Unlike forwards/futures, there is no obligation to exercise.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: (writing options for premium). Unlike forwards/futures, there is no obligation to exercise.

questions.question: Define beta in the CAPM equation.
questions.solution_html:
• Beta (β) is the measure of systematic (market) risk of a security or portfolio relative to the
  • market portfolio. In the CAPM equation: Expected Return = Rf + β (Rm – Rf) β = 1 →
  • moves with market; β > 1 → more volatile; β < 1 → less volatile.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: moves with market; β > 1 → more volatile; β < 1 → less volatile.

questions.question: Explain the parties in a swap contract.
questions.solution_html:
• A swap involves two counterparties who agree to exchange cash flows. In an interest-rate
  • swap, one party (fixed payer) pays a fixed rate and receives a floating rate; the other
  • (floating payer) does the opposite. No principal is exchanged (notional principal only).
  • Parties are typically a bank/financial institution and a corporate client.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: Parties are typically a bank/financial institution and a corporate client.

questions.question: Explain the slope of the CML.
questions.solution_html:
• The slope of the Capital Market Line (CML) is (E(Rm) – Rf) / σm (market Sharpe ratio). It
  • represents the additional expected return per unit of total risk (standard deviation) for
  • efficient portfolios combining the risk-free asset and market portfolio. Steeper slope =
  • better risk-return trade-off.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: better risk-return trade-off.

questions.question: Define variance.
questions.solution_html:
• Variance is a statistical measure of the dispersion of returns around the mean (expected)
  • return. It is the square of standard deviation and quantifies total risk (systematic +
  • unsystematic) of an investment. Formula: σ² = Σ (Ri – R̄ )² / n.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is the Dow Jones Theory?
questions.solution_html:
• Also known as Dow Theory, it is a technical analysis framework stating that the market
  • moves in three trends (primary, secondary, minor). A primary trend is confirmed only
  • when both the Dow Jones Industrial Average and Transportation Average move in the
  • same direction. The market discounts all known information.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: same direction. The market discounts all known information.

questions.question: What is the assumption regarding investor behaviour in CAPM?
questions.solution_html:

  • expected return and systematic risk (beta). They have homogeneous expectations and
  • can borrow/lend at the risk-free rate.
